doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Photo session: wagons, parades and goodbyes
title: Wagons, the lake camp and the Reese's candy company
summary: Laine says he did wagon work and built a camp at the lake for Reese's men, playing there on Sundays.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Yeah, we had loaned those pictures to somebody.
I don't know. I think Charles Smith reproduced part of that.
Yeah.
This funny one here with the little tiny...
Them days, they used to have wagons all around Connaughtry delivering packages.
You know, they're like, they have the trucks. It used to be wagons.
No automobiles enough for trucks or anything. Deliveries. All horse stuff.
For those stores.
And I used to do all their work, pretty much. Yeah. Blacksmith and play music, too.
Play music, too. Yeah. This funny little house here, little cottage, is that out at the lake? Yeah, that's at the lake.
That's... You might remember the James J. Reese's candy play people? I've heard of that thing. That's members from the Reese's candy place.

My camp is alongside of it. I built this place for James J. Reese's. That is, they bought almost off of me, understand? I was building this place. Now, them boys are from Reese's. The whole bunch in there from Reese's.
The bunch that are standing out in front of them. Yeah. With the holding a picture. And it's like they got a jug there. It says it was taken... On a Sunday... Hospital suite.
On a Sunday when I wouldn't, you know... At least a Saturday night when I wouldn't have a job that would require me to go on... I'd go over there and work.
Yeah.
See? Sunday I'd play a picnic, I'd be out at the lake.
That's the only one bad picture that they ain't dated.
All my instruments there.
Yeah.
Bad. All I done, pick up and go over.
That's all. This one with the string band out at the lake, too, you can see. Yeah. Out at the lake, yeah. Out at the camp.
That's at the lake, yeah.
Somebody holding a string bass and a guitar. Yeah, string bass, yeah.
Uh-huh.
I don't know what else. There's a lot of kids sitting down in front.
